chunks: And this report is not contradicted by what was narrated: Al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah from Salih and Ubays ibn Hashim from Thabit ibn Sharih from Dawud al-Abzari from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who bought a female slave and kissed her. He said, 'She becomes prohibited to his son.' And he said, 'If he had sexual intercourse with her (freed her), she is prohibited to his son.'

Because this report is understood to refer to when he kissed her with lust, in which case she becomes prohibited to the son. And we understand the first report to refer to when he kissed her without lust, in which case it is permissible for him to contract marriage to her, and there is no contradiction between the two reports.

key_terms.جَرَّدَهَا: he had sexual intercourse with her / freed her

ai.seo_question: Does a father's kiss of his female slave prohibit his son from marrying her?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction (takhfīf) between two narrations by distinguishing between kissing with lust (shahwah), which renders the slave woman permanently prohibited to the son, and kissing without lust, which permits the marriage contract. This jurisprudential nuance highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on intent and the specific conditions of 'tamkin' (availability for intercourse) in establishing kinship by pleasure (kināmah bi al-shahwah).
